title: Cosmetics and the token machine
summary: R.E.P.O. gives out player cosmetics from their own machine in the shop: you spend currency, the machine spins a display, and a cosmetic token comes out at one of four grades.
body: The shop has a machine for cosmetics, and it behaves like a dispenser rather than a shelf: you put currency in, the machine spins a display in front of you, and a cosmetic is handed over at the end.

What you receive is a token. The game keeps its tokens in four grades, and each grade has its own colouring, so an uncommon pull and a rare pull do not look the same even before you put either of them on.
The handover is staged rather than instant. The machine has its own animation and a confetti effect for the moment a cosmetic is revealed, and the reveal runs on a screen that spins up, then settles.

Wearing a cosmetic is about the avatar rather than the whole character. The player figure is split into parts that each carry a default surface, and a cosmetic is laid over those surfaces, which is why a hat lands on the head instead of covering the body.
You are not stuck with what you pull. A cosmetic can be hidden again, and the game keeps a menu for your avatar as well as its own interface for the tokens and for cosmetic objects in the world.
What this entry does not tell you: what a spin costs, the odds of each grade, or how many cosmetics the game ships. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The shop contains a machine that gives out player cosmetics.
Cosmetics are handed over as tokens, and the game keeps tokens in four grades.
The machine spins a display, settles on a result and celebrates it.
A cosmetic is its own asset, laid over the avatar's base surfaces.
The avatar is split into parts, so a cosmetic is applied to a part such as the head, the body, an arm or a leg.
facts.evidence: identifiers: Cosmetic - Head Top Mesh - Default, Cosmetic - Body Top Mesh - Default, Cosmetic - Arm Left Mesh - Default, Cosmetic - Leg Left Mesh - Default

facts.claim: A cosmetic can be hidden again, and the game keeps its own interface for tokens and cosmetic objects.
Bandages are an overlay of their own, named as a cosmetic among the layers the avatar wears.
The cosmetic side ships icons of its own for clothing and for colour.
